result.description:
Our Company

TerraCom Limited (ASX: TER) is an Australian based mining resources company with a global footprint, comprising a large portfolio of operating assets in Australia and South Africa within the coal sectors. We are a renowned low-cost producer focused on delivering exceptional outcomes from our high yielding diversified asset portfolio for its investors. TerraCom owns and operates the Blair Athol Coal Mine, in Central Queensland. This open-cut thermal coal operation consists of a full suite of mining activities inclusive of dragline, truck and excavator, dozer push, mine site rehabilitation, coal processing, coal crushing, product haulage and train load-out activities.

The Blair Athol Coal mine is located 24km northwest of the family-friendly township of Clermont in Central Queensland, 120 km northwest of Emerald and 275km southwest of Mackay.

TerraCom supports our people to grow, learn and develop their skills to reach their potential. We offer an exciting working environment, with career progression opportunities, as we truly believe that the capability and performance of our people is key to our success. Blair Athol Mine believes in fostering and nurturing each of our team members by providing them with a safe and enjoyable place to work, along with guidance and support from a leader they can rely upon. Come and play a key role in shaping our future!

The Role

We are currently seeking a highly motivated Surveyor Assistant / Technician to join our team at Blair Athol. You will assist the Surveyor in providing support for survey control to facilitate execution of mine activities including topsoil, stripping, overburden removal, coal mining, drilling/blasting, rehabilitation and associated projects around the mine. The right candidate will also forge a pathway towards further qualifications within the mine engineering team.

Responsibilities of the Role will include:

* Provide survey services and set out control points to ensure the accurate location and layout of work within the limits, offsets, grades, profiles and elevations for all mining related processes in accordance with the mine design criteria
* Conduct survey operations with drones, laser scanners and GPS and process the data to meet the required schedules
* Process survey data accurately and complete volume quantities
* Measure distances, angles and variations across site as directed
* Identify & escalate any non-conformance or processes that require corrective action.

Skills and Experience:

* A good work ethic, great communication skills and a desire to learn and grow
* A strong commitment to safety
* Survey or operational experience within a civil or mining environment
* Ability to prioritise and schedule work
* Ability to accurately measure and interpret data
* Competent user of MS Office tools

Benefits

* A fantastic opportunity to expand your mining career and join a great team offering exposure to all areas of operations and become part of the community in which you work.
* An attractive remuneration package in line with experience.
* An inclusive and supportive team culture.
* Excellent opportunity for career development

Note we thank all applicants for their interest, however any communications will be with short listed candidates only. No agency applications accepted.

From high-end custom kitchens and exclusive master closets to elegant libraries and unique home theatres, we are capable of turning your vision into a reality. Let us define your environment, enrich your living space and increase the value of your property with our timeless installations. Our in-house interior design team will also help with the selection of colours, countertop materials and the placement of your cabinets.

We have years of experience renovating kitchens and bathrooms, building and remodelling homes, and updating commercial spaces. During this time, we’ve built a reputation for solving problems creatively and thinking outside the box. You can bet we’ll get the job done quickly and efficiently.

We are seeking highly skilled Cabinet Makers to join our dedicated team of professionals.

As a Cabinet Maker you will fabricate, assemble, repair, and install custom wooden cabinetry, counters, and furniture. Interpret blueprints, operate woodworking machinery, and assemble components with precise hardware. The work involves selecting materials, applying finishes, and ensuring the final product meets both aesthetic and functional requirements.

The role includes but is not limited to:
Study blueprints, sketches, and work orders to determine specifications to create custom cabinet, counters, and furniture
Choose appropriate materials such as timbers, plywoods, veneers, particle board, synthetic wood, and other engineered wood products and estimate the total costs of the materials
Plan an effective approach to work to ensure that each project is completed on time
Cuts, shapes and assembles materials to build cabinetry and fittings
Utilise and control CAD and CNC machines to precisely mark out, cut and shape components
Apply finishes to cabinetry and fittings for aesthetics
Apply protective coatings to cabinets and furniture fitting hinges, locks, catches, drawers, shelves and other associated hardware
Collaborate with clients and tradespeople for accurate installation
Install cabinetry and fittings in various areas as directed
Repair or refurbish damaged cabinetry and fittings

To be considered for this role, you must have the following:
Trade qualified with proven experience in the same field
Knowledge in operating wide range of hand tools and power tools
Strong attention to detail and the ability to conduct quality checks on completed work
Ability to meet tight deadlines without sacrificing workmanship
Ability to work independently or as part of a team to complete assigned tasks
Knowledge of safety procedures and regulations to prevent accidents and injuries in the workplace
Physically fit and able to lift large, heavy equipment and materials
Attention to detail
Strong communication skills
Excellent reporting skills
Self-motivated, organised, punctual and reliable
Must have great work ethics

If you meet the above criteria and would like to be considered for this position, please apply now!
Salary: Between $79,499 and $82,000 per annum + Super

result.description:
Domino's Woodford is a busy, community-minded store in the heart of Woodford, QLD, serving freshly made pizzas, sides, pasta and desserts that arrive fast, taste great and hit the mark every time. As part of Australia's most recognised pizza brand, the store has built a loyal local following through convenient ordering, dependable quality and warm, friendly service. Behind the counter, the culture is energetic and customer focused, with team members encouraged to take ownership, develop their skills and enjoy coming to work. With the store continuing to grow, we are now seeking an experienced and motivated Retail Manager to lead our team, strengthen service standards and keep day-to-day operations running seamlessly.

Key Responsibilities
•	Recruit, induct, train and mentor team members, including shift runners, in-store crew and delivery drivers, and oversee rostering, shift supervision and individual performance across all trading hours.
•	Serve customers in store, over the phone and through online ordering channels, guiding them through the menu, recommending products, meal deals and options to suit their needs, and resolving enquiries and complaints promptly and professionally.
•	Oversee food preparation and order flow during peak periods so that product quality, order accuracy and delivery and pick-up times consistently meet Domino's standards.
•	Shape the store's product range and menu focus around national campaigns and local customer demand, set appropriate stock holding levels for ingredients, beverages and packaging, and define the service standards the team delivers on every shift.
•	Prepare and manage the store budget, setting sales targets, keeping labour and food costs within plan and identifying opportunities to improve profitability.
•	Maintain a safe and compliant workplace by upholding workplace health and safety obligations and food safety and hygiene standards across the kitchen, front counter and delivery operations.
•	Develop and implement the store's purchasing and promotional policies, manage supplier ordering, and set and adjust pricing on menu items, deals and offers within franchise guidelines.
•	Promote the store and its menu to grow order volumes and brand presence in the Woodford area, executing national marketing campaigns and building local initiatives such as school and sporting club partnerships, community sponsorships and social media engagement.
•	Maintain accurate records of stock movements, daily takings, banking and other financial transactions, completing wastage logs, reconciliations and end-of-day reporting through the store's point-of-sale systems.
•	Manage opening and closing procedures, cash handling and store security, and keep equipment well maintained with any faults addressed promptly.
•	Monitor sales results, service times and customer feedback, using store reports to identify and implement operational improvements.
•	Work closely with the franchise owner and the wider Domino's network on new product launches, technology updates and store initiatives.

Skills and Experience
•	A qualification at AQF Associate Degree, Advanced Diploma or Diploma level; a business, management, retail or hospitality discipline will be highly regarded.
•	At least one year of experience in a supervisory or management role, ideally within retail, hospitality or quick service restaurants.

Personal Attributes
•	A natural people leader who motivates by example and stays calm and decisive under pressure.
•	Energetic and hands-on, with a real enthusiasm for fast-paced service environments.
•	A customer-first mindset and pride in getting every order right, every time.
•	A clear and confident communicator who builds rapport with team members and customers alike.
•	Well organised, with strong attention to detail and sound commercial judgement.
•	Reliable, accountable and adaptable, with a proactive approach to solving problems.

What We Offer
•	A full-time position of 38 hours per week.
•	A salary of $75,000 to $85,000 per annum plus superannuation.

How to Apply
If you are ready to take the lead at a thriving local store, we would love to hear from you. Please apply with your current resume and a short cover letter outlining your management experience and why you would be a great fit for Domino's Woodford. Applications will be reviewed as they are received, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

 Apply now
 Job no: 944946

 Location: Eyre and Western

Eyre and Far North Local Health Network, Cummins 

Salary: WHD2 $1,204.70 - $1,226.60 per week (Pro-rata)+ 12% Superannuation + Leave Loading and Salary Sacrifice Benefits

Temporary Part-time position working 18 hours per week (up to 1 August 2028)

Overview

At Cummins Multi-Purpose Service, every shift leaves a mark - on a meal served with care, a clean room, a resident who feels seen. This part-time maternity leave contract (concluding 1 August 2028) offers flexible hours that can be negotiated to suit school commitments, making it a genuine opportunity for someone looking to contribute meaningfully to regional healthcare without compromising family life.

What the Role Involves

As a WHD2 Services Assistant within the Eyre and Far North Local Health Network, you'll move across a range of hands-on tasks that keep Cummins MPS running smoothly for the community it serves.

Preparing, delivering, and serving nutritious meals in line with individual dietary and care requirements

Maintaining cleanliness across the facility through housekeeping and laundry duties

Providing respectful, attentive service to clients, residents, and staff throughout each shift

Upholding food safety, infection control, and safe work practices at all times

What You'll Bring

A flexible, willing approach to varied tasks across different service areas

Strong communication skills and the ability to work respectfully with people from diverse backgrounds

Practical knowledge of food safety, housekeeping, and laundry processes

An understanding of confidentiality and the ability to meet deadlines in a care environment

Reliability and attention to detail that keeps spaces safe and welcoming

Experience in a healthcare or aged care setting, consistent with SA Health's commitment to safe, person-centred service delivery

Life at Cummins MPS

SA Health is built on the values of respect, integrity, and care - and at Cummins MPS, those values show up in the everyday. You'll be part of a close-knit team where your contribution is visible and genuinely matters to the people relying on local services in this regional community. As a public sector employee, you'll have access to salary packaging options, career development pathways, and the stability of working within South Australia's public health system. Regional health work offers something many roles simply cannot replicate: a direct, meaningful connection to the place and people you serve.

How to Apply

This is a part-time position based at Cummins MPS, Eyre and Far North Local Health Network, offered as a maternity leave contract through to 1 August 2028. Hours can be negotiated to suit school schedules. Submit your application through the SA Health careers portal, and if you'd like a conversation about the role before applying, contact the hiring manager listed in the job details.

About Us

With its ancient outback landscapes, boutique vineyards, oyster farms and Australia's best-kept-secret surf coast, Eyre and Far North will inspire and energise you.

The Eyre and Far North Local Health Network (EFNLHN) is responsible for the planning and delivery of hospital and health services over 337,626 square kilometres, taking in the Eyre Peninsula, western part of South Australia and north to Coober Pedy. We are one of the largest LHNs by area in Australia and communities include Ceduna, Cleve, Coober Pedy, Cowell, Cummins, Elliston, Kimba, Oodnadatta, Port Lincoln, Streaky Bay, Tumby Bay and Wudinna.

Services include acute care, medical, accident and emergency, surgery, birthing and midwifery, specialist consultancy, renal dialysis, chemotherapy, transfusions, rehabilitation, residential and community aged care, respite care, transitional care packages, Aboriginal health, mental health, allied health, community health, community nursing, palliative care, community home support packages and home modifications.

Click here to learn more about living and working in Eyre and Far North Local Health Network.

Why Join Us

Make a real difference and feel like an important part of the community. Being part of Eyre & Far North means you will be supported both personally and professionally, can take advantage of education and training opportunities, will have access to flexible working hours and be part of an inter-professional approach to holistic health care.

Salary package a range of benefits (including living expenses such as mortgage, rent, utility bills and groceries) up to $9,010 each FBT year + $2,650 for Meal Entertainment expenses each FBT year Click here more information

Wellbeing and counselling support: support for you and your family via our free Employee Assistance Program

Relocation support: relocation reimbursement of up to $15,000 may be available to people relocating for this opportunity. More information available from SA Health Careers - Relocation support.

Employee recognition: supportive and collaborative work environment where your contributions are valued and recognised.

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

SA Health is committed to providing an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity and inclusion for all employees. We strongly encourage applications from people of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander descent, culturally diverse backgrounds, members of the LGBTIQA+SB community and people who live with disability and-or neurodivergence.

We are committed to making workplace adjustments to provide a positive and supportive work environment. You are encouraged to let us know if have any support or access requirements during the recruitment process and beyond to ensure you can perform at your best.

Applicant Information

The South Australian public sector promotes diversity and flexible ways of working part-time. Applicants are encouraged to discuss the flexible working arrangements for this role.

Appointment will be subject to a satisfactory Criminal History Check and appropriate immunisation requirements.

Check(s)

National Police Certificate (NPC) for employment involving unsupervised contact with vulnerable groups required for this position (E.g. aged care employment or work involving vulnerable clients)

Immunisation Risk for this position is - Category A (direct contact with blood or body substances)

SA Health Services are required to implement the Addressing vaccine preventable disease: Occupational assessment, screening and vaccination policy in the workplace.
